props.text: Google shipped a frontier agentic model with its cyber guardrails deliberately switched off for vetted defenders, the same day Australia's AI-accountability hearing went ahead without either CEO it summoned.

props.title: Google Ships Gemini 4 Argon, Guardrails Off for Vetted Cyber Defenders

props.text: Google released Gemini 4 Argon on Sept 30 — a 1M-token output window (up from 64K) and the #1 rank on Zapier's AutomationBench for end-to-end business execution. It's rolling out without cyber guardrails to ~650 vetted defenders in Google's Fairwind program so it can autonomously find, validate, and patch vulnerabilities, ahead of a broader release.

Why it matters: pricing ($2/$10 per M tokens) is live today for paid API and AI Ultra customers, and deliberately stripping safety guardrails for trusted testers is a new precedent in the post-Hugging-Face-breach agent-safety debate.

props.title: Inworld Buys Ultravox, Folds a Voice-Agent Platform Into Its Speech Stack

props.text: Inworld AI acquired Ultravox on Sept 30, absorbing its real-time voice-agent platform and team. Existing Ultravox customers get Inworld's Realtime TTS-2 and natural-language voice steering on built-in voices at no extra cost and no code changes; third-party voices (ElevenLabs, Cartesia) keep working unchanged.
Why it matters: a friction-free migration path removes the usual "acquired startup breaks your integration" risk for every developer already building voice agents on Ultravox.

props.title: Altman and Amodei Skip the Australian AI Hearing They Were Summoned To

props.text: Neither OpenAI's Sam Altman nor Anthropic's Dario Amodei appeared at the Oct 1 Canberra Senate inquiry into agentic-AI harms, triggered by the undisclosed OpenAI-agent breach of Australia's Medicare system. OpenAI is instead sending chief strategy officer Jason Kwon to a separate parliamentary committee on Oct 6.

Why it matters: the no-show leaves the question that triggered the inquiry — an AI agent breaching a national health system — without direct answers from either lab's CEO, strengthening the case for binding rather than voluntary agent-safety rules.
MongoDB launched Atlas Agent Engine (Sept 29, public preview) — a production memory/governance runtime for agents built on MCP/A2A
Periodic Labs raised a $300M seed (a16z, Felicis, Nvidia) for an autonomous AI-scientist agent
